3. Plaint case, in short, is that one Tamej Sheikh was owner in possession of 3 decimals of land including the suit land, which was accordingly record in his name in CS Khatian No. 315. Tamej Sheikh transferred said land to Nandalal Das and Bateswar Das, sons of Mohan Das and delivered possession. SA record of rights was separately prepared in their names. By a registered deed of sale dated 24-12-69 Nandalal Das then transferred the suit land to Md Chan Miah. Md Chan Miah by registered sale deed dated 22-12-76 transferred said land to Alimul Hyder and handed over possession. When Alimul Hyder was thus owner in possession, he by two separate deeds of sale dated 27-6-81 and 15-11-82 transferred the suit land to the plaintiff and delivered her possession. The plaintiff got her name mutated and possessed on payments of rents. 

 4. The suit land was then recorded first in the name of Chan Miah in RS Khatian and then as khas in the name of the government. Defendant No. 2 Additional Divisional Commissioner (Revenue) served a notice dated 30-12-90 upon the husband of the plaintiff asking him to vacate the land by 30-1-91 otherwise he would be evicted therefrom by removal of unauthorised structures. Such notice cast a doubt over the title of the plaintiff who was accordingly, constrained to institute the suit. 

 7. In support of her case, plaintiff examined three witnesses including her husband and adduced number of documents, which were marked as Exhibit 1 to 9 while the defendant examined one 'Tahshilder' and adduced a copy of RS Khatian, which was marked as Exhibit 'Ka'. 

 12. The plaint case is that the suit land originally belonged to one Tamej Sheikh and CS record of rights was accordingly, prepared in his name. CS Khatian No. 315, Exhibit 1 recorded the suit land comprising of CS plot No. 828 as 'Nal'. Nature of tenancy was recorded as 'Borga Korfa' under land receiver Durga Sundari Basu and others. The appellant Court took the view that such tenancy held as 'Barga Korfa' had no 'raiyati' right, had no right to transfer before the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 came into force. He however, did not mention any law or authority in support of his view. 

 19. Plaintiff adduced original title deeds of Chand Miah and Alimul Hyder, Exhibits 3 and 4. She also adduced SA Khatian No. 787 which recorded the suit land in SA plot No. 2859 as 'Chandina' in the names of Nandalal and Bateswar, Exhibit 2.
